overview: Erik Knutsson was Swedish king who defeated Sverker II and restored the Erik line. The profile is anchored by concrete turning points: 1208 — Wins at Lena; 1210 — Secures rule after Gestilren.
He died in 1216, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Overview

He died in 1216, and his reign belongs to the wider story of Scandinavian state formation, Christianization, dynastic conflict, and northern Europe’s ties to England, the Baltic, and the Empire.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Erik Knutsson was born c. 1180. His family background is usually placed in House of Erik, though early Scandinavian genealogy can be uncertain and politically shaped.
Erik Knutsson's early life belonged to the medieval Scandinavian world, where kinship, sea routes, church contacts, assemblies, and armed followings shaped the opportunities available to a ruler.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Erik Knutsson of the Erik dynasty is remembered for decisively defeating his Sverker rival, winning the throne at the Battle of Gestilren in 1210 and bringing a measure of stability to the Swedish monarchy. The sources present him as the victor in a critical round of the dynastic war and as the first Swedish king recorded as formally crowned and anointed, a mark of the growing alignment of monarchy and church.

His reign was relatively secure by the standards of the period, and his coronation signalled an effort to put royal authority on a firmer, more sacral footing. He died of illness rather than violence, an unusual fate for kings of his contested line.

The personal character is thinly recorded, but the documented achievements — military victory, a stabilising reign, and the symbolic step of a church coronation — define how he is remembered. He is the Erik king who won and consolidated, his individual temperament largely hidden behind the dynastic and institutional record.

contentSections.title: As king of Sweden
paragraphs: Erik Knutsson survived earlier dynastic violence and defeated Sverker II at Lena. His reign restored the Erik line and reshaped Swedish succession politics.
As King of Sweden, Erik Knutsson had to turn dynastic claim into workable authority through alliances, military pressure, church support, and acceptance by regional elites.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died in 1216 at Nas Castle, leaving a young heir and prolonging Swedish dynastic instability.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: He is remembered as “the Survivor” and as a ruler whose victory helped define the Erik-Sverker rivalry.
Later saga, saintly, or national traditions often amplified Erik Knutsson's reputation, so the article separates near-contemporary evidence from later memory where possible.

timeline.title: Born
timeline.description: Erik Knutsson was born around c. 1180, but the birthplace is not securely recorded. The date is approximate, but it places the early life in the setting of Kingdom of Sweden.

timeline.title: Wins at Lena
timeline.description: Erik Knutsson defeated Sverker II’s forces at Lena, a key victory in Sweden’s dynastic wars.

timeline.title: Secures rule after Gestilren
timeline.description: After Gestilren in 1210, Erik secured kingship more firmly and became the first Swedish king known to have been crowned.

timeline.title: Death
timeline.description: Died in 1216 at Nas Castle, leaving a young heir and prolonging Swedish dynastic instability.

timeline.title: Aftermath and memory
timeline.description: Erik’s reign helped stabilize the Erik dynasty after decades of conflict with the Sverker line, and his crowned kingship became part of Sweden’s developing royal ceremony.
